fact: NOAA's Storm Events database logged 48 High Wind events from 2011 through 2025 in the National Weather Service forecast zone for Larimer County below 6,000 feet and northwest Weld County, 44 of them between October and April.
quote: WFO = BOU, CZ_TYPE = Z, CZ_FIPS = 38 (LARIMER COUNTY BELOW 6000 FEET / NW WELD COUNTY), EVENT_TYPE = High Wind, 2011–2025: 48 events · begin month October–April: 44 · MAGNITUDE ≥ 65 kt: 15 · largest 83 kt MG (2025-12-19, event 1302336: "Peak wind gust of 95 mph was recorded 3 miles south of Carter Lake.")
source_label: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details files 2011–2025 (NWS forecast zone 38, High Wind)
notes: Counted 2026-09-25 from the yearly details files (d2011–d2025): STATE = COLORADO, WFO = BOU, CZ_TYPE = Z, CZ_FIPS = 38, EVENT_TYPE = High Wind; 47 distinct begin dates. Zone entries, one per zone per episode, so a count of NWS-logged high-wind events, not of windy days. Town assignment is by the zone's name (Larimer County below 6,000 feet), an inference; Windsor and Johnstown straddle the county line and are left out. Carter Lake is outside NoCo's town list: do not present the 95 mph gust as a town event.

fact: NOAA's Storm Events database logged 30 High Wind events from 2011 through 2025 in the National Weather Service forecast zone for central and southern Weld County, 26 of them between October and April.
quote: WFO = BOU, CZ_TYPE = Z, CZ_FIPS = 43 (C & S WELD COUNTY), EVENT_TYPE = High Wind, 2011–2025: 30 events · begin month October–April: 26 · largest 70 kt MG (2011-12-31, event 357346)
source_label: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details files 2011–2025 (NWS forecast zone 43, High Wind)
notes: Counted 2026-09-25 from the yearly details files, same filter as zone 38 with CZ_FIPS = 43; 30 distinct begin dates. Zone narratives name gusts near Greeley, Evans-area stations, Eaton, Severance, Johnstown, Mead, Milliken and Firestone, which is the basis for applies_to (an inference from the zone name and narratives).

fact: NOAA's Storm Events database lists peak gusts of 84 mph in Loveland and 65 mph in Wellington in the high-wind event that began on November 29, 2019.
quote: Peak wind gusts included 84 mph in Loveland and 65 mph in Wellington.
source_label: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details file 2019, event 865032 (NWS forecast zone 38, High Wind, Nov. 29–30, 2019)

fact: On December 15, 2021, NOAA's Storm Events database lists peak gusts of 79 mph near Loveland, 78 mph near Johnstown and 71 mph near Mead.
quote: Peak wind gusts included 83 mph near Natural Fort Rest Area and 79 mph near Loveland. … Peak wind gusts included:  78 mph near Johnstown, 71 mph near Mead, 68 mph near Briggsdale, and 67 mph near Nunn and Severence.
source_label: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details file 2021, events 992641 and 992646 (NWS forecast zones 38 and 43, High Wind, Dec. 15, 2021)
notes: "Severence" is NOAA's spelling in the narrative.

fact: NOAA's Storm Events database lists a 73 mph gust at Severance and 61 mph at the Greeley airport on January 16, 2026, and gusts of 85 to 95 mph across northern Larimer County on March 12, 2026.
quote: Wind gusts reached 55 to 70 mph with a few gusts of 70 to 75 mph. Here are some of the stronger wind reports. At Severance 73 mph, Greeley Airport 61 mph,  near Masters 71 mph, and 60 mph near Keenesburg. … Extreme high winds occurred across northern Larimer County with several gusts in the 85 to 95 mph, very high wind speeds for the plains.
source_label: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details file 2026 (c20260918), events 1302377 (zone 43, Jan. 16, 2026) and 1320017 (zone 38, Mar. 12, 2026)
notes: The 2026 file (created 2026-09-18) runs through June 2026 and NOAA may still revise it; recheck the two narratives before relying on them after the next file update.

fact: The National Weather Service defines high wind as sustained winds of 40 mph or more lasting an hour or longer, or winds of 58 mph or more for any duration.
quote: Sustained wind speeds of 40 mph or greater lasting for 1 hour or longer, or winds of 58 mph or greater for any duration.
source_label: National Weather Service glossary, High Wind

fact: The Colorado Climate Center says places at the western edge of the plains very near the mountains get periodic, severe turbulent winds when high westerly winds cross the mountain barrier, called chinook winds when they warm and bora winds when they come with a strong cold front.
quote: At the western edge of the plains and near the foothills of the mountains, there are a number of significant changes in climate. Average wind movement is less, but areas very near the mountains are subject to periodic, severe turbulent winds from the effects of high westerly winds over the mountain barrier. These winds are sometimes referred to as "chinook winds" when they warm, and "bora winds" when they are associated with a strong cold frontal passage downslope off of the mountains.
source_label: Colorado Climate Center, Climate of Colorado

fact: PolyTurf's landscape installation manual says its sand infill cushions impacts and acts as ballast to hold the turf in place.
quote: The infill also provides impact absorption and is a ballast to hold the turf in place.
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping (2015)

fact: PolyTurf fastens turf edges to a plastic-lumber edging board around the perimeter to prevent creep (rippling) or curling, and screws the turf to it so the turf can be tightened if it ripples or moves with heat and cold.
quote: Recycled Plastic Lumber (RPL) Edging Board: 1x6’s or 2x4’s laid around the perimeter of the installation flush with the underlay to nail the outer edges of the turf to prevent creep (rippling) or curling in high use areas or when deemed necessary. Use plastic lumber (used for decking) when available or alternatively you may use redwood for rot resistance. Turf should be screwed into the edging board to allow for tightening of material if rippling occurs or when expansion/contraction occurs.
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping (2015)

fact: PolyTurf advises against pressure washing its turf because it displaces the sand infill.
quote: It is not recommended to pressure wash the turf, as this will displace the sand infill.
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping (2015)

fact: PolyTurf's manual says the ground under turf must be firm enough not to move, or it creates humps and valleys or collects drainage water.
quote: The sub-strate needs to be firm so that it doesn’t move around under the turf, creating humps and valleys or collecting drainage water.
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping (2015)

fact: PolyTurf advises keeping the scraps from the original installation to patch areas that are damaged later.
quote: It’s always a good idea to keep the scraps left over from your original installation. They can be used to patch any areas that become damaged.
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping (2015)

fact: Shaw's ShawGrass installation guidelines suggest landscaping nails every 4 to 8 inches along the perimeter of a lawn without edging, to keep the edges from lifting.
quote: If you are not going to apply an edging, we suggest you hammer landscaping nails every 4” to 8” along the perimeter of your synthetic lawn to prevent the edges from lifting.
source_label: Shaw Industries, ShawGrass Installation Guidelines (PDF), Secure Edges

fact: Shaw describes a buried edge: a narrow trench along the border, the turf's edge tucked into it and nailed, the soil backfilled and compacted, and the edge hidden under mulch, straw or rock.
quote: C. Buried Edges. Excavate a narrow trench around the border, deep enough to bury the exposed edge of the turf. Tuck the turf’s edge into the trench (additional trimming of excess turf may be necessary). Nail and backfill the excavated soil against the buried turf, and compact. The edge can then be hidden with mulch, straw, rock, etc.
source_label: Shaw Industries, ShawGrass Installation Guidelines (PDF), Secure Edges

fact: Shaw's guidelines say infill helps weigh the turf down and keeps the fibers upright.
quote: Infill helps weigh the turf down and stabilize the fibers to keep them upright and prevent matting.
source_label: Shaw Industries, ShawGrass Installation Guidelines (PDF), Infill

fact: Shaw tells installers to roll turf out the day before so it can relax, to lay wrinkled turf flat in the sun or stretch it, and to plan on about 18 inches of waste because turf nearest the core of the roll may be excessively wrinkled.
quote: Roll out the turf the day before installation as this will allow the panel to relax. If the synthetic turf has wrinkles, lay it flat on a flat surface in the sun or stretch. … Also, remember that turf wrapped closest to the core may be excessively wrinkled, plan on about 18” of waste just to be on the safe side.
source_label: Shaw Industries, ShawGrass Installation Guidelines (PDF), Turf

fact: SYNLawn's DIY guidelines recommend about 1 to 2 pounds of sand infill per square foot and say the sand acts as ballast and helps protect the turf from UV.
quote: We recommend about 1-2 lbs. of sand per sq. ft., depending on the application and the product. The sand acts as ballast and helps protect from UV rays.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (PDF)

fact: Integriturf's installation guide trims the stretched turf cleanly along the border so there are no large gaps between turf and border and no long overlap left to trim.
quote: Trim the edges: Once the turf is stretched, trim the perimeter edges of the turf using a utility knife or scissors. Take your time to cut the turf edges cleanly along the border (usually concrete or bender board) so that you don't end up with large gaps between the edge of the turf and the border, or long over lap that will require further trimming.
source_label: Integriturf, Synthetic Turf Installation Guide (PDF)

fact: Integriturf's installation guide leaves unrolled turf in direct sunlight for a few hours so the backing and fibers relax and flatten.
quote: Unroll the synthetic turf and let it sit for a few hours in direct sunlight to allow the backing and fibers to relax and flatten out.
source_label: Integriturf, Synthetic Turf Installation Guide (PDF)

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council's buying guide for landscape turf says infill is needed to help keep an installation from moving, because its evenly spread weight minimizes the turf's expansion and contraction with temperature.
quote: Infill is needed to help keep the synthetic grass installation from moving-infill provides an even distribution of weight that will minimize the expansion and contraction of turf when the temperature changes.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013), Guidelines for Infill

fact: Synthetic Grass Warehouse's installer column removes the infill to reach the nails or staples before re-stretching turf, and warns that fasteners rust-bond to the compacted base, so pulling them carelessly tears fibers out of the backing and leaves divots.
quote: Prior to removing the wrinkles you must remove the infill so that you may reach the nails/staples. … When the moisture from the subgrade materials comes in contact with nails or staples that have been placed, Oxidization occurs and creates a rust/bond to the compacted soil. If you are not careful when pulling up nails or staples you will pull fibers from the backing of the turf. If this happens it will cause the surface of the turf to have “Divot” marks and you will end up replacing the entire section.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Preventing Wrinkles in Turf

fact: The same column says that once turf has been down more than 3 months, trying to pull a wrinkle out may do more damage, and adding ballast or cutting the wrinkle out may fix it instead.
quote: If your turf has been down more than 3 months you may do more damage to the turf by trying to remove them. You may try to ballast or cut out the wrinkle which may rectify the problem.
source_label: Synthetic Grass Warehouse, Ask JW: Preventing Wrinkles in Turf

fact: Firestone's maintenance standard says artificial turf areas may not contain uplifted surfaces, among other deterioration, and damaged areas must be repaired or replaced to match the existing turf.
quote: iii. Artificial turf areas shall not contain weeds, holes, tears, stains, discolorations, seam separations, uplifted surfaces, heat degradation, depressions, odors, excessive wear, or similar deformities and measures of deterioration. Damaged or worn areas shall be repaired or removed and replaced in manner that results in consistent appearance with the existing artificial turf.
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.4.F.2.f.iii (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 through the Municode API (Supplement 38, job 488870, product 18062), the text behind the library page.
